_instruction: Drug Product Composition — name, quantity (metric), function, quality. Table g: category_header + sub_tests grouping mandatory.

components.title: Composition summary
components.prompt: ESSENCE: Short composition summary (Label/Value grid). Product name, Each ... contains, API strength, Excipients q.s. No full formula.
components.example: {"columns": ["Label", "Value"], "rows": [{"Label": "Product Name", "Value": "[from source]"}, {"Label": "Each hard gelatin capsule contains:", "Value": ""}, {"Label": "[API]", "Value": "[strength]"}, {"Label": "Excipients", "Value": "q.s."}]}

components.title: Name and quantity stated in metric weight or measures, function and quality
components.prompt: ESSENCE: Full unit formula — each ingredient with metric quantity, pharmacopoeial/quality standard (Specifications), and function. CONTRACT: Top-level rows array only. MANDATORY GROUPING — each process stage is exactly ONE parent row: empty Ingredients/Specifications/Qty/Function strings, category_header = stage name, sub_tests = array of ingredient child rows. Required category_header blocks in order: Dry mix → Binder Preparation → Prelubrication → Lubrication. Then ONE standalone row: Ingredients='Total Fill Weight', Qty = fill material total mg. Then category_header Capsule Shell with sub_tests (shell composition, size, colour). Last standalone row: Total Capsule Weight (filled). FORBIDDEN: flat ingredient list without category_header parents. Child rows use keys: Ingredients, Specifications, Qty. / Capsule in mg, Function.
components.example: {"columns": ["Ingredients", "Specifications", "Qty. / Capsule in mg", "Function"], "rows": [{"Ingredients": "", "Specifications": "", "Qty. / Capsule in mg": "", "Function": "", "category_header": "Dry mix", "sub_tests": [{"Ingredients": "Apixaban", "Specifications": "IH", "Qty. / Capsule in mg": "2.50", "Function": "Active substance"}]}]}

components.title: Abbreviations
components.prompt: ESSENCE: Expansions for pharmacopoeial and in-house abbreviations used in the composition table (e.g. BP, IH, q.s.).
